> AI code review — automated review for reference; please use your judgment.

- packages/tui/src/prompt/slash-command-match.ts:4 — sensible design: only kicks in for queries ≥3 chars, only when nothing prefix-matches, and caps edit distance at 1 (Damerau-Levenshtein covers transpositions like "udno"→"undo"). Guards prevent it from hijacking normal prefix behavior.
- packages/tui/src/prompt/slash-command-match.ts:14 — typo candidates are prepended ahead of existing fuzzy matches; combined with the `.slice(0, 10)` in autocomplete this can displace legitimate fuzzy results when several commands are within distance 1. Probably acceptable given the small candidate set, but worth knowing.
- packages/tui/src/prompt/slash-command-match.ts:38 (`damerauLevenshtein`) — correct full-matrix implementation including transposition; O(n·m) per name per keystroke is fine at command-list scale.
- Nit: the `<= 1` threshold is a magic number — a named constant (`MAX_TYPO_DISTANCE`) would document intent.
- Tests cover preserve/fallback/reject cases well, including the short-query bypass.

> AI code review - automated review for reference; please use your judgment.

- packages/core/src/subagent.ts:126 - `description="${input.title}"` is interpolated unescaped into the synthetic XML payload; a title containing quotes or angle brackets corrupts the `<subagent>` structure that parents/consumers parse. Escape or use attribute-safe encoding.
- packages/core/src/subagent.ts:113/119 - `Effect.catchTag("Session.SyntheticConflictError", Effect.die)` turns an addressable race into a fiber death; consider logging + skipping the notification instead, since losing one notice is recoverable while a defect may not be.
- packages/core/src/session.ts:613 - model fallback chain now ends at `session.model` (previously undefined), so commands targeting non-subagent agents also inherit the sessions current model where they previously left selection untouched; confirm that side effect is intended since it changes switchModel behavior on the normal command path too.
- Good extraction of duplicated subagent orchestration into one module; new session-command test covers admit/job/notification wiring end to end.

> AI code review — automated review for reference; please use your judgment.

- Coordination flag: this deletes `packages/core/src/plugin/provider/amazon-bedrock.ts` and `azure.ts` as "unreachable," while two other open PRs in flight actively extend exactly those files (#43231 Bedrock Mantle support, #43515/#43135 Azure DeepSeek adapter). Please reconcile with those authors before merging — either they're building on dead code (they should retarget), or these paths aren't actually unreachable.
- packages/core/src/model-resolver.ts:188 — behavior change worth a release note: `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` without a `baseURL` is now hard-unsupported instead of falling through to the (removed) plugin's defaults. Configs that relied on implicit defaults will start erroring.
- The inlined OpenAI-compatible handling in the resolver keeps the `Auth.none/bearer` distinction; the new resolver tests cover it — good replacement coverage for the deleted plugin tests.
- Large test deletions (~1500 lines) match the removed surface 1:1 from what I can see; no blocking issues beyond the coordination question above.

> AI code review - automated review for reference; please use your judgment.

- packages/tui/src/routes/session/index.tsx:2802-2805 - clean guard via `finiteNumber`; note negative exit codes (signal deaths) will render as e.g. "exited with code -15", which is accurate but may confuse users expecting 128+n conventions - optional nicety only.
- No blocking issues found.

> AI code review — automated review for reference; please use your judgment.

- packages/opencode/src/lsp/server.ts:1968 (`PureScriptLS`) — follows the existing HLS pattern correctly (which-guard, `--stdio`, cwd); config registration and `.purs` extension mapping are both wired up.
- Nit: root markers cover spago/psc-package/bower but not `purs.json`; harmless since NearestRoot falls back gracefully, just a completeness thought.
- No blocking issues found.

> AI code review — automated review for reference; please use your judgment.

- packages/core/src/session/model-transport.ts:243 — correct classification: close code 1009 means the server rejected without processing, so mapping it to `"rejected"` (rather than ambiguous) makes HTTP retry safe.
- packages/core/src/session/model-transport.ts:427 (`Stream.catch`) — sticky per-session `httpFallback` is the right call: once a payload has exceeded the peer's limit, every larger exchange would fail too. Conservative even across reconnects, which seems intended; a comment stating "never resets for the session lifetime" would lock that in.
- packages/core/test/session-model-transport.test.ts:548 — strong test: asserts the second request short-circuits to fallback without reopening the socket (`opened` stays 1), which pins exactly the sticky behavior.
- Nit: the log message says "using http" but doesn't include the session ID or payload size threshold; adding sessionID would help correlate in multi-session logs.
- No blocking issues found.

> AI code review — automated review for reference; please use your judgment.

- packages/ai/src/protocols/anthropic-messages.ts:992 (and openai-chat.ts:696, bedrock-converse.ts:675, open-responses.ts:1015) — `Schema.decodeUnknownSync(Schema.Json)(event)` will *throw* if any rest-captured field isn't JSON-representable, and since these run inside error-construction paths (`onError`, `step`) a throw would mask the original provider error. Prefer `Schema.decodeUnknownOption(...)`/`decodeUnknownExit` and fall back to `null` — matches the repo guidance to avoid sync-decode throws in fallible paths.
- packages/ai/src/schema/events.ts:219 — inconsistency: reason classes treat `data` as optional, but `ProviderErrorEvent.data` is required. Any producer constructing this event without a payload now fails validation; consider making it optional there too unless you want to force callers to always attach something.
- The `StructWithRest` + `Record(String, Unknown)` pattern to keep unknown fields through parsing is the right call — that's what makes preserving e.g. `request_id` possible at all.
- Test updates across all four protocols pin exact `data` round-trips including nested objects; good coverage.

> AI code review - automated review for reference; please use your judgment.

- packages/client/src/promise/service.ts:137 - `typeof value.pid !== "number"` is redundant after `Number.isInteger(value.pid)` (which implies number); harmless but can be dropped for clarity.
- packages/client/src/promise/service.ts:183-194 - the legacy/modern disambiguation (legacy must lack version+pid) correctly prevents a partial modern body from being accepted as legacy; the negative conditions are dense but tested.
- Test coverage for malformed registrations and primitive/partial health bodies is thorough - good security hardening against corrupted/hostile registration files.

> AI code review — automated review for reference; please use your judgment.

- packages/core/src/plugin/provider/local-reasoning.ts:20 (`infer`) — name-based heuristics ("gpt-oss", "deepseek-v4", "qwen3", "gemma-4") are inherently a maintenance list; consider a brief comment inviting updates as new local reasoning models ship. Also note "deepseek-v4" won't match ids like "deepseek-r1-distill-v4" unless substring rules intend that (they do match substrings — fine, just confirm).
- packages/core/src/plugin/provider/lmstudio.ts:78 — LM Studio reports a reasoning `default` option but `fromOptions` ignores it; if the server marks e.g. `default: "on"`, no variant reflects that. Minor, but surfacing the default in variant ordering or docs would help.
- packages/ai/src/providers/openai-compatible.ts:79 — `reasoningEffort` is emitted as `providerOptions.openai.reasoningEffort` for *any* OpenAI-compatible endpoint; stricter servers may 400 on unknown body params. It's opt-in via settings, so acceptable — just ensure docs say which servers honor it.
- Variant gating looks right: ollama requires the "thinking" capability, vLLM returns [] for unknown models, and tests pin all three providers including negative cases (nomic-embed excluded).
- Docs updates for ollama/lmstudio/vllm match behavior.

> AI code review - automated review for reference; please use your judgment.

- packages/tui/src/routes/session/rows.ts:360-369 - `tokens = output - 1` assumes the first token lands at `time.started`, but if providers include reasoning tokens in `output` (there is a separate `reasoning` field), the rate blends visible + hidden generation while tests call it "visible output throughput". Confirm the semantics or subtract reasoning too.
- packages/core/src/session/runner/publish-llm-event.ts:498-505 - `generated` is captured at step-finish receipt time (before flush); under bus backpressure this slightly understates true completion time - acceptable for a display metric, worth a comment.
- packages/core/src/session/message-updater.ts:198-199/254 - retry resets of started/generated plus the `??=` on text.started keep the window idempotent across replays - good.
- Weighted summary aggregation (sum tokens / sum durations) instead of mean-of-rates is the right call; guards against tiny windows (<250ms) avoid noisy values.

> AI code review — automated review for reference; please use your judgment.

- Scale note: with ~140 files of translations across dozens of locales, individual strings aren't verifiable here — please ensure your existing key-parity/CI checks cover all locales for the new keys (`session.background.*`, `settings.workspaces.*`, etc.) and consider a native-speaker pass for the higher-traffic surfaces.
- packages/app/src/components/settings-v2/providers.tsx:139 — regression risk: the catch handler previously surfaced the underlying `err.message` and now shows a generic "failed to disconnect {{provider}}" toast. Users debugging auth/provider issues lose the actual reason (e.g. network vs 403). Consider logging the original error or including it when present.
- packages/app/src/context/language.tsx:223 (`backgroundTasks`) — good implementation of the new AGENTS.md rule: one typed operation owns plural selection + composition, and callers just pick move/running phrasing.
- packages/app/src/context/server-session-v2-reducer.ts:149 — attaching `{ notice: "instructions", instructionSources }` metadata is a behavior change beyond i18n; test was updated accordingly, but any consumers filtering on `metadata === undefined` may need review.
- Nice touch using Unicode isolates (`\u2068...\u2069`) in the Arabic strings for bidirectional safety.

> AI code review - automated review for reference; please use your judgment.

- packages/core/src/aisdk.ts:733-735 - `/ 100_000_000_000` encodes the AIU-to-USD rate as a magic number; add a comment naming the source/spec (and the implied $0.01 per AIU) so future billing changes are traceable.
- packages/core/src/session/usage.ts:41-47 - trusting provider-reported cost means a misconfigured/malicious endpoint can report 0-cost usage that overrides catalog pricing everywhere (session totals, console billing views). Reasonable tradeoff for accuracy on OpenRouter/Copilot, but consider clamping or flagging large divergences from calculated cost.
- packages/core/src/aisdk.ts:686-687 - resetting `state.cost = undefined` after finish keeps multi-step streams correct; note the value is captured once and reused for both stepFinish and finish events of the same step - intended and consistent.
- Tests cover OpenRouter streamed cost, Copilot nano-AIU normalization, NaN/negative fallback - good coverage.

> AI code review — automated review for reference; please use your judgment.

- Security consideration: nothing prevents `--no-auth --hostname 0.0.0.0`, which exposes an unauthenticated opencode server to the network. Since this flag exists precisely for sandboxed/container use, consider either refusing the combination or printing a prominent warning when auth is off and the address isn't loopback.
- packages/cli/src/env.ts:17 — `OPENCODE_AUTH=false` silently disables auth for every future invocation when set in a shell profile; worth documenting prominently in troubleshooting/security docs since it's an easy footgun to forget about.
- packages/server/src/process.ts:179 — `ServerAuth.required(auth)` gating both lifecycle control (`stop`) and app dispatch is consistent; note that with auth disabled anyone who can reach the port can stop the daemon — acceptable given the feature's purpose, but part of the same exposure story as above.
- packages/cli/src/server-process.ts:125 — correctly avoids writing/echoing a password when auth is off, and `register` omits the field rather than writing `null`; make sure all info-file consumers tolerate its absence (the schema change suggests yes).
- Test covers unauthenticated `/api/health`; consider one more asserting the lifecycle endpoint also respects the disabled-auth path.

> AI code review - automated review for reference; please use your judgment.

- packages/core/src/snapshot.ts:270-273 - `lockFailure` matches English-only git error strings (`index.lock|another git process|...`); users running a localized git (LANG=de/fr/zh) will never match, so stale index.lock falls into the no-backoff path and retries hammer git every capture. Consider matching the errno/exit code or checking for an existing `<file>.lock` on disk instead of parsing text.
- packages/core/src/snapshot.ts:135-137 - `retryAt`/`retryMs` are plain mutable fields updated from concurrent fibers without synchronization; two overlapping failed captures can interleave reads/writes (benign today since worst case is a missed backoff extension, but worth noting).
- The double-checked `retryAt` (outside + inside the lock) is a good pattern to avoid lock contention while preventing stale admissions.
- Tests cover lock-timeout retry with TestClock and stale index.lock recovery including asserting the lock file survives - strong coverage.

> AI code review - automated review for reference; please use your judgment.

- packages/core/src/git.ts:13-14 - git is resolved at module import time and cached forever; a user installing/repairing Git while opencode runs keeps the stale path until restart, and every process start pays a `which` scan even when Git features go unused. Lazy resolution on first use (memoized) would avoid both.
- packages/util/src/cross-spawn-spawner.ts:265-270 - the native-spawn guard (win32 + no shell + absolute + .exe/.com) is correctly narrow since cross-spawn still handles .cmd/.bat argument escaping; consider a comment noting why shell usage must keep using the shim (quoting rules).
- Fallback to bare `"git"` when `which` misses preserves prior behavior - good.
- No tests for the resolution logic; at least a unit test pinning the `.com/.ext` set behavior would help since it gates a security-sensitive spawn path.

> AI code review — automated review for reference; please use your judgment.

- Consistency question: `command.session.record-notes` / `.description` are added verbatim in English to ~120 locale dicts (am, ar, az, bg, …) while `fa` is the only one I can spot with an actual translated string. If the others are placeholders, they'd be better omitted so the en-dict fallback applies (and future translation PRs don't need to touch 120 files); if they're meant to ship translated, most locales currently render English.
- The fa translations look reasonable; per repo guidance, terminology ("سشن" for session) may warrant a native-speaker check.
- Key placement is consistent (grouped with other `command.session.*` entries) across files — good mechanical hygiene.
- No blocking issues found beyond the untranslated-copy question.

> AI code review - automated review for reference; please use your judgment.

- packages/tui/src/routes/session/index.tsx:2944 - demoting block-tool errors from the error color to `subdued` reads as intentional (denials are expected outcomes, not system failures); just confirm genuinely unexpected errors on this surface (e.g. renderer crashes) are not also routed through `error()` and silently de-emphasized.
- No blocking issues found.

> AI code review — automated review for reference; please use your judgment.

- packages/tui/src/util/stdio-guard.ts — well-built primitive: exact-original restoration, callback handling in both argument positions, sink isolation via try/catch, 0600 perms enforced post-open (umask-proof), and a hard byte cap so a chatty plugin can't fill the disk.
- packages/tui/src/app.tsx:194 — smart placement detail in the comment: releasing the guard before the fatal-error print means crash output still reaches a restored stderr. Worth keeping that invariant in mind if scope structure changes.
- Nit: two concurrent opencode instances share `stdio-main.log` with `truncate: true`, so instance B startup wipes instance A's captured output. A pid-suffixed filename would avoid the clobbering.
- packages/opencode/src/cli/tui/worker.ts:14 — worker realm gets its own log file, good separation; if `rpc.dispose` never runs (hard crash) the fd stays open until process exit, which is fine but worth knowing.
- Test suite covers the failure modes I'd worry about (throwing sink, unopenable file, limit accounting across installs) — excellent coverage.

> AI code review - automated review for reference; please use your judgment.

- packages/app/src/pages/home/home-sessions-model.ts:26-31 - the synthesized fallback project uses the *sessions* directory as worktree, so two sessions from different subdirectories of the same unadded project render as separate projects (separate avatars/names). Grouping by session.projectID first would keep them together when metadata is available.
- packages/app/src/pages/home/home-sessions-controller.tsx:23-25 - `projectMetadataByID` reads `home.server.focusedSync()?.data.project`; verify this sync data exists before any project list fetch completes, otherwise early renders synthesize projects from empty metadata and names flicker once loaded.
- Good extraction of the pure builder into a tested model module with coverage for both scoping modes.

> AI code review — automated review for reference; please use your judgment.

- packages/opencode/src/tool/registry.ts:152 (`question`) — good bridge reuse: plugins get the exact same modal + answer pipeline as the built-in question tool, including tool-call attribution via `callID`.
- Contract check worth confirming: the JSDoc promises rejection "if the user dismisses the modal" — verify `Question.Service.ask` actually rejects (vs resolving empty) on dismissal, since a resolve-with-empty would silently hand plugins `[]` answers and break that documented behavior.
- packages/app/src/pages/session/composer/session-question-dock.tsx:111 — prefill guards are right: skips when custom mode already on or field non-empty, and the `customOn` latch prevents re-filling after the user deliberately clears the text. Nice.
- packages/plugin/src/tool.ts:41 — `QuestionAnswer = ReadonlyArray<string>` reads like a single answer list per question but the method returns an array of these (one per question); consider naming it `QuestionAnswers` or documenting the outer/inner distinction to avoid misuse.
- Schema addition is optional and backward compatible in both v1/v2; SDK types regenerated accordingly.

> AI code review — automated review for reference; please use your judgment.

- packages/app/src/context/permission.tsx:322 — good security posture: `write-notes` is excluded from all auto-approve paths so notebook mutations always get human review, matching the PR's interactive-review intent.
- packages/app/src/pages/session.tsx:2119 (`onSaveLearnings`) — the instruction prompt is hardcoded inline and names the `notes_commit` tool literally; if the tool is ever renamed or gated behind a plugin, this silently degrades to a confusing no-op prompt. Consider centralizing the prompt string (and ideally asserting the tool exists) somewhere testable.
- Design note: `.note.yaml` per folder plus a root-level gitignore entry here only covers this repo; users' own projects need their own ignore rule for committed notebooks — worth documenting since memory files may contain session-derived content some teams won't want committed.
- The diff was too large to fully review (34 files); I focused on the app/permission/i18n surfaces. Recommend dedicated human attention on the server-side `notes_commit` tool validation and YAML parsing paths (js-yaml load of untrusted-ish files can construct unexpected objects unless using safe load / schema validation).
- i18n keys added for en; assuming other locales follow via the translation pipeline (see #43066 pattern).

> AI code review - automated review for reference; please use your judgment.

- packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/stats.ts:~150 - `stats.models.slice(0, limit)` truncates silently; add a "+N more" footer so users know the table is clipped (toolUsage table has the same issue).
- packages/cli/src/commands/handlers/stats.ts:~110-125 - activity heatmap math is solid (Monday-aligned, 52-week clamp), but `weekStarts` length uses `(dateOrdinal(end) - dateOrdinal(start)) / 7` which can produce one extra column at exact week boundaries; harmless visually, worth a glance if alignment ever looks off.
- Good privacy posture: default card omits cost and tool names, verified by tests asserting absence of `private_tool`/cost in default output.
- Flag validation (mutual exclusion of --days/--year/--all, --limit >= 1, year bounds) is thorough.

> AI code review — automated review for reference; please use your judgment.

- packages/opencode/script/opencode_d:17 — portability nit: `readlink -f` isn't available on macOS < 13 or Alpine busybox. A POSIX-friendlier fallback (`cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd -P`) would make the symlink-resolution work everywhere.
- packages/opencode/script/opencode_d:25 — UX trap: the wrapper unconditionally consumes `$1` as the target directory, so `opencode_d run "hello"` (a natural typo) silently treats `run` as a path and fails confusingly. Consider defaulting to `$ORIGINAL_PWD` when `$1` starts with `-` or matches a known subcommand.
- packages/opencode/bin/dev.ts — the splice-then-import approach is clean; note it also mutates `argv` for anything that inspects `argv[2]` later, which is exactly what you want here.
- CONTRIBUTING.md section is clear and includes both the manual and wrapper paths.

> AI code review - automated reference; please use your judgment.

- packages/app/src/components/titlebar.tsx:186-206 - `rootSession` walks parents with sequential awaits per hop; a deeply nested subagent chain means N round-trips before the tab highlights. Consider caching resolved roots per server or accepting the brief unhighlighted window explicitly (it currently degrades to "no active tab", which is fine).
- packages/app/src/components/titlebar.tsx:196-205 - the `resolved?.session.id === input.route.sessionId` staleness guard correctly avoids cross-route contamination during refetch; nice handling of the async resource race.
- E2E coverage now includes the nested-grandchild case and asserts exactly one visible tab stays active - good regression protection.

> AI code review — automated review for reference; please use your judgment.

- packages/opencode/src/util/archive.ts:9 — strong fix: moving paths out of the interpolated command string into env vars eliminates both the literal-path breakage (`'`, `[`, `]` in names) *and* a PowerShell injection vector the old quoting had. `-LiteralPath` is the right parameter.
- packages/opencode/test/util/archive.test.ts:7 — good regression case with apostrophes and brackets in both source and destination names. Since the body early-returns off-Windows, confirm Windows CI actually runs this suite, otherwise it's dead coverage locally.
- Nit: consider asserting that a malicious-looking name like `foo'; Remove-Item -Recurse ~; 'bar.zip` also extracts safely — that's the property this fix really guarantees.
- No blocking issues found.

> AI code review - automated review for reference; please use your judgment.

- packages/tui/src/routes/session/index.tsx:2310 - `opaque` keys off presence of `part.state`, not specifically `reasoningEncryptedContent`; if a provider populates state with other fields while leaving content genuinely empty (not encrypted), the row will claim "encrypted" incorrectly. Matching on the encrypted-content field would be more precise.
- packages/tui/src/routes/session/rows.ts:243-249 - appending on `reasoning.started` makes empty reasoning visible during streaming - good; confirm the appended part gets cleaned up if the provider ends with neither content nor state (row would linger as an empty group).
- Disabling hover/expand for opaque parts avoids dead interactions - good touch.

> AI code review — automated review for reference; please use your judgment.

- packages/opencode/src/plugin/azure.ts:118 (`discoverAzureModels`) — `.catch(() => ({}))` silently swallows every discovery failure, including RBAC denials and `az` not being installed. The user just sees an empty model list with no explanation; consider logging a warning (or surfacing the error message in the UI) so misconfiguration is diagnosable.
- packages/opencode/src/plugin/azure.ts:33 (`token`) — cache is keyed by scope only; if the user runs `az account set --subscription other` mid-session, requests keep using the old tenant's token until it lapses near the 60s refresh buffer. Probably rare, worth a comment or cache invalidation hook.
- The dummy 365-day `expires` on the stored oauth entry is clever (real freshness lives in the CLI), but it also means the client will never prompt for re-auth when `az login` itself has lapsed — the docs do call this out ("sign in again when the CLI session expires"), good.
- Scope routing in `scopeForRequest` (foundry vs cognitiveservices by hostname/path) is well-tested, including header stripping of `api-key`/`x-api-key` while preserving unrelated headers.
- Test suite is excellent — mocked shell/fetch seams, negative cases (discovery failure keeps startup alive), and exact az command assertions.

> AI code review - automated review for reference; please use your judgment.

- packages/core/src/tool/runtime.ts:34-45 - the null-stripping retry is a good fix for `X | null` advertised optionals; note it also masks genuinely invalid *combinations* (a null somewhere unrelated plus a real type error elsewhere gets one extra attempt). Harmless since the original error is preserved when the retry fails, but worth knowing the error reported may be from the first attempt while the retry also failed differently.
- packages/core/src/tool/runtime.ts:96-103 - `isForeignSchema` via `ast instanceof SchemaAST.Base` is a neat cross-instance discriminator; add a comment that it intentionally flags same-version duplicate installs too (the warning text already covers remediation).
- packages/plugin/src/effect/tool-schema.ts:31-36 - converting outputs through `Schema.flip` so validation runs Type->Encoded matches the hosts encode path - correct directionality, and the test asserting `jsonSchema.output.required` locks it in.
- packages/tui/src/context/local.tsx:236-244 - resource key includes models count so provider connect triggers refetch - thoughtful; note `model.default` failures are swallowed to undefined which yields the old "No provider selected" behavior, acceptable.
- Tests are excellent across all three fixes, including the real dual-instance fixture.

> AI code review - automated review for reference; please use your judgment.

- packages/core/src/session.ts:1135-1147 - `inheritModelVariant` logic is sound (explicit wins, inherit if supported, else "default"); one nuance: when neither command nor session/input has a variant, the result is an explicit `"default"` rather than undefined - confirm downstream treats explicit default identically to unset (it looks like yes, but worth locking with an assertion).
- packages/core/src/session.ts:1143-1145 - catalog miss (`model` undefined) silently downgrades to default; a transient catalog load could drop a supported variant. Consider retrying or treating unknown models as variant-compatible.
- This rewrites the exact region PR #42415 (subagent background commands) also modifies - flagging likely merge-conflict/rebase coordination between the two.
- Test matrix covering all five inheritance cases plus plugin-flush ordering is thorough.
Any progress on this?  I'd accept a work around at this point, but as it is it seriously wastes a ton of screen real estate.

This issue might be related to an existing open issue. Please check:
- #40613: also reports `forceRequired` being `false` when it should be `true` in `git worktree remove` scenarios, and also causes the same `project-copy.test.ts` assertion to fail — though the root cause there is locale-based regex matching rather than `instanceof` identity across duplicate module copies. The two issues may interact or overlap in fix scope.
Any news on this? I don't think i'm the only one needing to run 5+ MCP servers at all times, and the token overhead is brutal, especially Linear MCP.

Not a duplicate of #40613, though the symptom is the same. That one is a locale problem: the regex in git.ts that computes forceRequired only matches English git output, and git is spawned without any locale pinning. This one is an identity problem: the handler uses instanceof to recognise the error, which returns false when @opencode-ai/core is loaded twice in a process.

They're independent — fixing either leaves the other. Both have to go for forceRequired to be reliable.

I kept the `fs.isDir` check intentionally. `InstanceStore.load` may return a cached context after the directory is deleted, and a missing child can resolve through an ancestor repository rather than fail. Therefore, letting `store.load` handle the not-found case would not cover the regression. I added a regression test for the cached-instance/deleted-directory case and documented the reasoning. Thanks — both reviews were helpful. Addressed in `f0b62b095` (fix(llm): coalesce message logger output and honor log levels) with a few deliberate deviations noted below.

**1. Double logging in `generate()` — fixed.** Dropped the post-fold log in `generateWith`; the response is now logged exactly once when the terminal event passes the stream pipeline, which also covers `stream()` consumers (the session's native runtime). Verified by test: exactly one `LLM request` and one `LLM response` entry per `generate()` call.

**2. Per-event fragmentation — fixed, with a twist: the AI SDK path had the same bug.** `packages/opencode/src/session/llm.ts:~415` had an identical per-event `Stream.tap` (always at `logInfo`, one entry per delta) that neither review flagged. Both paths now use a new `MessageLogger.responseStream(model, level)` combinator: deltas accumulate and a single coalesced `LLM response` entry is emitted when the terminal event (`finish` or `provider-error`) passes through. I chose terminal-triggered emission over timer coalescing: it's exact (one entry per response, no tail loss, no cross-turn attribution) and non-terminal events pay only for an array push.

**3. AI SDK path through `MessageLogger` — addressed as far as the data shapes allow:**
- The AI SDK request log now uses the same `MessageLogger.log(level, label, payload)` dispatcher (no more hard-coded `Effect.logInfo`) and the response log the same `responseStream` coalescing, over the `LLMEvent` stream the AI SDK parts are converted to via `toLLMEvents` — identical labels, payload shapes, and level semantics on both runtimes.
- Tool parts no longer collapse to `[tool-call]` placeholders: `tool-call(name): JSON(input)` / `tool-result(name): JSON(output)`.
- Where I'm pushing back: **the raw provider body for `trace` is not obtainable on the AI SDK path** — the AI SDK constructs the wire body internally and `opencode` never sees it (the Copilot `includeRawChunks` is a different, provider-specific thing). So on that runtime `trace` ≡ `debug` content, now documented in a comment at the site and in the config description. Similarly `formatMessages` itself can't be shared there: the AI SDK path formats `ModelMessage[]`, a different data shape from `LLMRequest` content parts, and there is no `LLMRequest` on that path to build one from.

**4. Tests don't observe log output — fixed.** The integration tests now install a capture logger (`Logger.make` sink + `Logger.layer`) and assert the emitted level, payload shape, exactly-once emission, coalesced delta text, generation params at `debug`, and the raw body at `trace`.

**5. `trace` → `logDebug` — fixed with one extra finding.** Tracing now maps to `Effect.logTrace`. But the runtime gap the second review suspected was real and worse than described: `minimumLogLevel()` in `packages/core/src/observability/logging.ts` had no `TRACE` env mapping (capped at `DEBUG`), and Effect's filter drops entries *less* severe than the minimum — so `logTrace` output would have been invisible even at `OPENCODE_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG`. Added `TRACE` to the env map; the config description now states the level requirements explicitly.

**6. `formatEvents` join — fixed, not the literal `\n` between segments.** Straight `\n`-joining would corrupt the response text, because text/reasoning deltas are fragments of one text (`"Hello"` + `" world"` → `"Hello\n world"`). It now accumulates consecutive deltas of the same kind (joined with `""`) and separates distinct segments (text, `[reasoning]:`, tool events, usage, `error:`) with `\n` — so `usage:` no longer glues onto the text and interleaved reasoning/text stays ordered. Unit-test expectation updated. One new behavior worth noting: `provider-error` terminal events now render as `error: <message>` in the response entry.

**7. Privacy note — done.** Config description now warns that logs can contain full transcripts including tool results.

Not a duplicate of #43126 — these are two layers of the same feature and I'd suggest keeping them linked rather than merged.

- #43126 defines the user-facing goal: when the provider reports a known reset time, persist + pause + auto-resume the session.
- #43324 specifies the engine half of that pipeline: how OpenCode *knows* when the next reset is and what to do while it waits.

Concretely, #43324 only covers the "wait until reset" decision (classified via retry-after + metadata.limitName, then slept on), not the suspend/resume plumbing itself (that's #27511's scope). It also adds a per-provider config schema so any fixed-window provider can declare its own schedule, rather than hardcoding the Go subscription limits into retry.ts as today.

So: #43126 = UX thread, #27511 = mechanism, #43324 = retry-engine config + reset scheduling. Happy to fold the config/proposal section into #43126 if maintainers prefer a single thread — just want the reset-scheduling logic to land somewhere.
